VIII. THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN LOCAL SHORT-TERM USES OF MAN'S ENVIRONMENT AND THE MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF LONG-TERM PRODUCTIVITY
Physically, man's environment will be impacted during the execution stages of the program. The impact will be minor due to the relatively small amount of heavy construction work and the phasing of activities over a two to three year period. Amounts of environmental pollution produced by project activities will be minimal. Economically, in the short-term, the tax base will be reduced due to taxable land coming under the public domain. Socially, some individuals and businesses will be inconvenienced by having to relocate.
However, in return for these short-term losses or inconveniences, the overall community will benefit. These benefits will come in the form of better streets and sidewalks, places for project residents to park near their homes, security provided by additional lighting, security for the area provided by the flood plain conservation activities, and generally a better neighborhood to live in. Neighborhood blight, excelerated by the flooding, will be averted through the property rehabilitation program. Gradually, the tax base will be adjusted to its original level by project induced property appreciation.
